articles.summary: Data centers are the largely unseen infrastructure behind modern life, powering everything from the apps on your phone and shows you stream to online shopping, banking and artificial intelligence . Inside these warehouse-sized facilities, thousands of servers store data, process digital requests and keep online services running around the clock. Most Americans may never see one, but they rely on them constantly, often without realizing it. "Data centers have been around for as long as technology has been around," Brittany Kaiser, CEO of Alpha Compute, told Fox News Digital. "Anytime you’re touching technology and using everything from social media to your email, all of that information, all of the data is being processed in a data center." As more of the economy moves online, data centers have become far more than a niche piece of the tech industry. They are increasingly essential infrastructure for everyday American life. The U.S. is home to roughly 4,000 operational facilities, with thousands more planned or under construction as demand for cloud computing and AI accelerates.
